foreignObject.div: Figure 10. The transform tier folds 40.9% of this corpus's bytes; the opcode's own term is 1.2% of the bits, and the whole spelling effect is 4.1%. Both arms are the same 1,000 scenes at 24,000 steps on the same byte codec, so their difference — 19.8 ±1.8 bits/drawing across seeds — is the spelling and nothing else. Split by position class: 11.15 for the copies the fold removes, 5.30 against it for the REPEATX and ENDREP it adds, and 14.0 ±1.7 on bytes that are byte-identical in both spellings. With the codec held fixed that context term can no longer be the alphabet: it is the fold's indirect consequence — a 41% shorter program predicts its own shared bytes better — resolving the earlier caption's “codec and sequence length” to the sequence length alone. The fold's own term is +5.84 ±0.18 across seeds and stays within 5.67–6.14 across three structured codecs. Ticks are half the seed range, and the dashed rule is the ISA's direct term.
